messages:
rachel: pushed a tiny Next.js starter that wires Redwood SDK + LangChain for quick RAG demos. internal repo: https://git.redwood.local/next-quick-rag
devon: nice. quickstart steps?
rachel: npm ci, copy .env.local, set REDWOOD_HOST and REDWOOD_API_KEY or run the dev auth helper. start with npm run dev.
priya: i ran it and hit intermittent failures: generate works but tracking/telemetry calls return 401 from browser requests.
devon: probable proxy issue. Are you using /api/proxy or calling REDWOOD_HOST directly from client?
rachel: using /api/proxy route to keep server token local. handler currently builds headers = {'content-type':'application/json'} and forwards body.
priya: that drops Authorization/cookie. Also saw that the client helper surfaces 429 without retry (node SDK does backoff). both together make the sample flaky under rapid eval runs.
devon: fixes: forward req.headers.authorization and req.headers.cookie if present; fallback to REDWOOD_SERVER_TOKEN env for server-side auth. add client fetchWithJitter retry util with capped exponential backoff.
rachel: agree. i'll add a minimal fetchWithJitter in src/lib/fetchRetry.js and wire the demo evaluate button to use it. example impl: ```async function fetchWithJitter(url, opts, retries=3){ for(let i=0;i<retries;i++){ const res = await fetch(url, opts); if(res.status !== 429) return res; await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, Math.min(1000, 200*Math.pow(2,i)) + Math.random()*150)); } return fetch(url, opts); }```
priya: also add default CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=300 in the sample's in-memory store to prevent local memory growth during repeated evals.
devon: and add scripts/eval-harness.js that can POST results to MOCK_TELEMETRY_URL (default file sink) and supports a --run-id flag so CI parallel runs don't clash.
rachel: plan: PR with proxy header forwarding, fetchWithJitter, cache TTL, eval harness and README update. will assign reviewers.
test-bot: ci/test triggered for branch rachel/next-quickfix (build 7)
priya: temporary workaround for folks: set REDWOOD_SERVER_TOKEN in .env.local so proxy adds Authorization header server-side.
devon: thanks, verified workaround works locally. :thumbsup:
rachel: opening PR now, will update here with link and CI status.
